verdicts.reason: Quote states the transfer behavior; scenario testable.
FIFO order stated; checkable by scoreboard and by assertion on data.
Quote says clocks may differ in frequency but must be synchronous; MAY with scenario is fine.
Quote says pointers cross without synchronizers (a design structure statement), not a prohibition; it is MUST (no synchronizers), not MUST_NOT. Structural, not checkable from interface.
Equal clocks is a normal use; MAY scenario.
Quote lists the interface features; scenarios exercise them.
Structural description of hierarchy; nothing observable to verify at interface level.
Description of module contents; no verifiable behavior.
Description of module contents; no verifiable behavior.
Description of the array implementation options; nothing to verify.
Any depth >=2 and width >=1 stated as required; scenario with non-power-of-two depths.
Feature is optional parameter selecting direct path or one retiming flop; it is an option, not mandatory behavior.
Gap-free streaming stated with condition; checkable by assertion and scenario.
Four-phase handshake required; checkable on handshake signals and by scenario.
Optional macro replacement is a configuration that can be exercised by running with the parameter set; check none is wrong, though it is only a wrapper option.
Required feature; scenario with different frequency clocks.
Required feature of exact full and empty boundaries; checkable.
Required feature; thresholds checkable against occupancy.
Required feature; overflow and underflow pulses checkable.
Required feature; show-ahead checkable.

questions.question: The quote does not define the exact latency or the exact static threshold values and how full/empty flags are timed across the two domains. Settle these before verification.
SF-1.1-06 lists a software reset with handshake while SF-1.1-14 requires a four-phase handshake. Should the reset behavior and its REQ-SRST requirements be specified in detail?
The clocks are required to be synchronous with a fixed phase relationship, but no behavior is specified if they are not. Is that in or out of scope?
